name: SQL Injection Through AI
title: SQL Injection Through AI
answer: SQL injection is the insertion of malicious query text into a database command, and it has a newer cousin in AI systems that generate SQL from user or document input. When a model turns natural language into a query, prompt injection can steer that generation toward harmful statements such as dropped tables, broad reads, or stacked commands. The generated SQL therefore needs the same controls as any untrusted input: least privilege, read only access where possible, and query review. This topic covers both the classic injection path and the model mediated path that produces it.

sections.body: SQL injection is the insertion of malicious query text into a database command, and it has a newer cousin in AI systems that generate SQL from user or document input. When a model turns natural language into a query, prompt injection can steer that generation toward harmful statements such as dropped tables, broad reads, or stacked commands. The generated SQL therefore needs the same controls as any untrusted input: least privilege, read only access where possible, and query review. This topic covers both the classic injection path and the model mediated path that produces it.
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body: The stack usually starts with a model or agent that receives a request, a schema description, and sometimes retrieved documents, then emits SQL that a driver executes against a database such as PostgreSQL.The database itself, its driver, and the connection credentials are the last line before a query runs. Every page on this site is itself built from a PostgreSQL database, so the pattern is common rather than exotic.
sections.heading: What it runs on

sections.body: Work begins by mapping where untrusted text can reach a query: chat prompts, uploaded files, web pages, and retrieved context all count. Teams then test generation paths with adversarial inputs, checking whether a model can be talked into unions, subqueries, comment tricks, or multiple statements. Defenses are layered, including parameterized queries, allow lists of tables and columns, read only roles, statement timeouts, and a review step before execution. Logging the generated SQL alongside the prompt that produced it makes failures reproducible.
sections.heading: How the work is done

sections.body: Ownership of generated SQL sits with the team that operates the database, not with the model provider, so access reviews and role design matter more than model choice. Provenance should record which prompt, document, or agent produced a query, and which credentials it used. Regulatory and audit expectations for data access apply the same way whether a human or a model wrote the statement. This is a description of practice, not legal advice, and any specific compliance question belongs with counsel.
sections.heading: Rights, risk and provenance

sections.body: Expect more agents holding database credentials, which widens the surface for prompt driven injection. Work is moving toward sandboxed query execution, schema aware validation, and policy engines that inspect generated SQL before it runs.The practical direction is to treat model output as untrusted input by default.
